text:
maria - customer: Hey team, since the model update this morning our p95 for /v1/generate jumped from ~450ms to ~1.2s and p99 is showing 2.7s. No change in request volume. Seeing a lot of latency complaints from internal users. Can you take a look?

ana - support: Sorry you're hitting this — I dug into the tenant logs. We rolled the quantization profile to `int8-fast` at 08:12 UTC as part of the rollout for model: redwood-xlarge-v2. Endpoint: /v1/models/redwood-xlarge-v2/generate. Posting the core lines from our timing logs: 

```
// sample timing snippet
2026-03-15T08:12:27Z model=redwood-xlarge-v2 profile=int8-fast seq_len=128 tokens=120 total_ms=1210
2026-03-15T08:12:28Z model=redwood-xlarge-v2 profile=int8-fast seq_len=64 tokens=40 total_ms=980
2026-03-15T08:12:29Z model=redwood-xlarge-v2 profile=fp16 seq_len=128 tokens=120 total_ms=460
```

ana - support: Customer says they only changed the quantization profile, no prompt changes. Repro steps attached.

maria - customer: repro: curl to /v1/generate with prompt "Translate to bullet points" 1k times, see p95 jump. Happy to give access to a test tenant.

james - eng-runtime: @li @ana thanks. Initial hypothesis: the int8-fast kernels are triggering fallback paths or extra dequantize/permute ops for the current compiled kernel selection. Could be kernel selection mismatch for sequence lengths we see. Also need to check KV cache alignment — quantized KV layout sometimes forces extra memcpy.

li - eng-ml: Good catch. I ran a quick local bench with the same model weights quantized to int8 using the new calibration. Observed similar wall-time increase on a T4-config. The int8 path reduced FLOPs but increased host-device copies by ~35% because the FP8->INT8 calibration we used added an intermediate staging buffer.

james - eng-runtime: Can you paste the quant config you used?

li - eng-ml: Here — snippet from the rollout config: 

```
quant_profile: "int8-fast"
calibration: "online"
fallback_to_fp16: false
quant_batch_threshold: 8
warmup_samples: 0
```

li - eng-ml: I think `warmup_samples: 0` is the culprit — we didn't perform representative calibration on KV/cache patterns. Online calibration is producing a shape-specialized kernel that causes path divergence.

ana - support: What's the quick mitigation to get customer back to p95 baseline?

james - eng-runtime: Fast mitigation options: 
- Roll back the quantization profile for that model route to `fp16` (hosted) — instant effect.
- Or enable `fallback_to_fp16: true` on the profile so slow requests take FP16 path.
- As an intermediate, reduce `quant_batch_threshold` to 1 to avoid batching that triggers the slow path.

li - eng-ml: For correctness and quality: if we want to keep int8 for cost, we should run a calibration job with representative prompts (warmup_samples >= 200), enable KV-aware quantization and a small canary rollout (5%). That should avoid the deopt.

ana - support: Can we do a tenant-scoped rollback today? Customer is high-priority.

james - eng-runtime: Yes. I can patch the routing policy for that tenant to pin model variant `redwood-xlarge-v2:fp16-v1` and set 100% traffic to it. I will also add a monitoring check to watch p50/p95/p99 for 30m post-change.

deploy-bot: deploy initiated by james - eng-runtime for tenant=acme-corp route=/v1/models/redwood-xlarge-v2, target_variant=fp16-v1, rollout=100% canary=false

james - eng-runtime: Done. Rollback completed at 08:35 UTC. Please confirm if p95 drops.

maria - customer: Confirmed — p95 dropped to ~470ms within a few minutes. Thanks, that fixed the immediate problem.

ana - support: Great. Follow-ups:
- li: own the int8 investigation + calibration job and report back with a safe config.
- james: add an automated preflight check in the rollout pipeline that detects KV-copy regression and refuses canary >0 until calibration passes.
- ana: open a postmortem and notify account team.

li - eng-ml: Will do. Plan: run calibration against 5 representative prompts across seq_len buckets (32, 64, 128, 256, 512), warmup_samples=500, enable `kv_aware_quant=true`, test in perf-lab with identical batch distribution, then 5% canary for 24h. Expect report in 48h.

james - eng-runtime: I'll add the preflight check. Quick pseudo-check: run 100 synthetic requests and compare p95 before/after profile switch, abort rollout if p95 regress > 20%. I'll wire that into the console as a gate.

ana - support: I'll file the customer-facing summary and link the internal findings.

maria - customer: Thanks team, appreciate the quick rollback and follow-up.

li - eng-ml: One more note — FP8 experiments were also touched in the same deploy metadata. FP8 still has unstable kernels on older GPUs; avoid enabling FP8 on T4s for now. We'll add an explicit hardware blacklist.

james - eng-runtime: Noted. Action items recorded: rollback done, preflight gate for quant rollouts, calibration job, hardware blacklist for FP8 on T4. Closing thread once PRs merged. :thumbsup:
